import Example from "../../../components/Example.astro";
import { ReadyCheck } from "../../../components/examples/ReadyCheck.tsx";

CSS custom properties are the theming API. Components reference semantic tokens, themes supply values, and games override them.

## Starting themes

| Theme    | Status    | Designed for                                                             |
| -------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Arcade   | Available | Competitive and action games: dark base, bright accents, chunky controls |
| Tactical | Planned   | Strategy and data-heavy games: restrained accents, compact spacing       |
| Playful  | Planned   | Casual and party games: brighter surfaces, rounded, larger controls      |

Apply a theme to any element and everything inside it:

```html
<html data-game-theme="arcade"></html>
```

Without a theme, components use neutral defaults.

## Overriding tokens

Override `--game-*` variables in your own CSS. Both examples below render the same `ReadyCheck` component; the second only changes tokens.

<div class="not-content example-side-by-side">
  <Example label="Arcade">
    <ReadyCheck client:visible />
  </Example>
  <Example label="Arcade with token overrides" class="example-neon">
    <ReadyCheck client:visible />
  </Example>
</div>

```css
.neon-arena {
  --game-bg: #0a0514;
  --game-surface: #150a2a;
  --game-panel: #1f0f3d;
  --game-primary: #7cf29a;
  --game-primary-contrast: #062611;
  --game-secondary: #9b5cff;
  --game-secondary-contrast: #0a0514;
  --game-border: #9b5cff;
  --game-focus-ring: #ff5ce1;
  --game-radius-md: 0;
  --game-radius-lg: 0;
  --game-border-width: 2px;
  --game-shadow: 0 0 16px rgb(124 242 154 / 0.35);
  --game-font-display: ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", Menlo, monospace;
}
```

Framework styles are in cascade layers, so your overrides win regardless of selector specificity. When you change a color that text sits on, also change its `-contrast` partner.

## Tokens

| Category   | Tokens                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Color      | `bg`, `surface`, `panel`, `primary`, `primary-contrast`, `secondary`, `secondary-contrast`, `danger`, `danger-contrast`, `success`, `warning`, `text`, `text-muted`, `border`, `focus-ring` |
| Typography | `font-body`, `font-display`, `font-size-sm`, `font-size-md`, `font-size-lg`, `font-size-xl`                                                                                                 |
| Shape      | `radius-sm`, `radius-md`, `radius-lg`, `border-width`, `shadow`                                                                                                                             |
| Spacing    | `space-xs`, `space-sm`, `space-md`, `space-lg`, `space-xl`                                                                                                                                  |
| Motion     | `duration-fast`, `duration-normal`, `ease`                                                                                                                                                  |

Each token is a CSS variable prefixed with `--game-`, such as `--game-panel`. Durations become `0ms` when the player prefers reduced motion.

## With Tailwind CSS

Import `@game-ui/themes/tailwind.css` after Tailwind to use tokens as utilities in your own game UI: `bg-game-panel`, `text-game-text`, `rounded-game-md`, `shadow-game`, `p-game-md`, and `font-game-display`.
